finalists.one_liner: Go with a new 30-bar extreme only when open interest has risen 5%+ over the same window.
finalists.why: Rising open interest on a breakout means new positions are being opened, and whoever opened against the move is trapped. The losers are faders who added against the breakout.
finalists.risk: More open interest also means more leverage to liquidate if the break fails: bigger and faster reversals.

finalists.one_liner: Once a day, hold the sign of the trailing 30-day return; 4-ATR disaster stop.
finalists.why: Time-series momentum is the best documented futures anomaly: under-reaction to news and trend-chasing flows make last month's sign persist. The losers are contrarians and late hedgers trading against the drift.
finalists.risk: V-shaped reversals: the sign only flips after much of the reversal has already happened.

finalists.one_liner: Close outside a tight 7-day range while the last day's volume runs 30% above the prior week: go with it.
finalists.why: A week-long balance area holds a lot of inventory; when price leaves it on rising participation the side caught inside has to exit over several days. The losers are swing traders positioned for the range to hold.
finalists.risk: Few signals, and a false break of a weekly range costs a full 2-ATR stop.

pairs.note: 87 setup x symbol tests at 5%: expect 4.4 to look good by chance (P(at least one) = 99%); the best of 87 zero-edge backtests is expected to show Sharpe ~1.43 over 3.0y. Bar to clear: Sharpe > 1.88 (Bonferroni) instead of 0.95.
